The central claim rests on standard optimal transport and convex analysis results (Brenier, lopsided minimax, Donsker-Varadhan), on domain assumptions about the cost and loss functions (Assumptions 1-2), and on two unproven algorithmic premises: the finite-sample Sinkhorn estimator faithfully represents the true penalty, and stochastic gradient ascent finds a good maximizer of the non-concave HyCNN objective. The main free parameters are the regularization, penalty, strong-convexity and smoothing coefficients, all tuned by hand or cross-validation.
